title: CAP
objectives: Explain CAP with measurable requirements and failure modes
During a network partition you choose consistency or availability; otherwise you trade latency vs consistency (PACELC).

cards.title: text
cards.body: CAP: under a partition (P), a system either rejects some requests to stay consistent (CP) or answers possibly-stale data (AP). Consistency models range from strong (linearizable) to eventual.

cards.title: text
cards.body: During a network partition you choose consistency or availability; otherwise you trade latency vs consistency (PACELC).

cards.title: diagram
cards.body:

Flow: Normal operation → Network partition → Choose: reject (CP) → or serve stale (AP) → Heal & reconcile

cards.title: text
cards.body: Saying "pick two of three" as if you can drop P. Partitions happen; the real choice is C vs A during one.

cards.title: animation
cards.body: Close by restating scope, numbers, and the main risk for CAP. During a network partition you choose consistency or availability; otherwise you trade latency vs consistency (PACELC).

title: Delivery Semantics
objectives: Explain Delivery Semantics with measurable requirements and failure modes
Retries are safe only when operations are idempotent; use keys, exponential backoff and jitter.

cards.title: text
cards.body: Networks fail mid-request, so clients retry. An idempotency key lets the server return the stored result for duplicates. Backoff with jitter prevents synchronized retry storms.

cards.title: text
cards.body: Retries are safe only when operations are idempotent; use keys, exponential backoff and jitter.

cards.title: diagram
cards.body:
Step through how a request moves.

Flow: Client sends key → Server checks key store → New: process & save → Duplicate: return saved → Client backs off on failure

cards.title: text
cards.body: Retrying immediately in a tight loop. That turns a small outage into a thundering herd.

cards.title: animation
cards.body: Close by restating scope, numbers, and the main risk for Delivery Semantics. Retries are safe only when operations are idempotent; use keys, exponential backoff and jitter.

questions.prompt: Why add jitter to retries?

choices.label: To avoid all clients retrying at the same instant

questions.explanation: Randomness spreads retries out.

questions.explanation: Exactly-once is a composed property with idempotency.
